headline: Adaptive and personalised models track non-stationary neural and cardiac dynamics
label: Neural Dynamics Model Validation
summary: Recent work probes whether fitted neural and cardiac models recover underlying dynamics when activity is non-stationary or patient-specific.
synthesis: The common thread is inference of underlying dynamics from recordings, paired with explicit tests of whether the fitted model is trustworthy. A discounted Poisson-Gamma model with Thompson sampling adaptively selects electrodes under a fixed channel budget to track non-stationary spontaneous activity in dissociated networks. A graph-computational framework with GNN system identification is applied to HD-MEA recordings of human cortical organoids, characterising evoked responses under repeated stimulation. Subject-specific whole-brain models fitted to resting-state fMRI in Alzheimer's disease indicate that distributed correction is needed, since optimal single-site stimulation sites are not the most affected regions. Bayesian history matching personalises reaction-eikonal electrophysiology models of 17 HCM patients from 252-electrode body surface potentials. What is new is the emphasis on personalisation and adaptive sampling as routes to validity, rather than model fit alone. The items differ in system and scale, so this reflects a shared methodological emphasis rather than a common finding.
